themes_detail.label: Tree Crisis Spike
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests and dead/dying tree complaints surged THIS WEEK to 3 and 7 respectively—a 2300% and 460% spike above 8-week baselines (3 vs. 0.1 avg; 7 vs. 1.2 avg)—suggesting either sudden storm damage, disease outbreak, or new resident awareness campaign worth investigating.
evidence: New Tree Request: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
Dead/Dying Tree: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.93)
Community Board budget records show repeated park/amenity reconstruction requests, indicating chronic tree maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Did recent weather event (wind, freeze) damage trees across Greenpoint/Williamsburg? Interview Parks Department and residents.
Are residents newly mobilized to report tree issues due to awareness campaign or social media coordination?

themes_detail.label: Noise at Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: House of Worship noise complaints hit 3 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 1100% spike above 8-week baseline (3 vs. 0.2 avg)—suggesting possible conflict around religious services, events, or amplified sound that may still be unresolved.
evidence: Noise - House of Worship: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
Signal is 2 weeks old; current week data not yet available—unclear if issue persists or resolved
Greenpoint/Williamsburg has diverse religious institutions; conflict likely involves specific venue or event
reporting_angles: Identify which house of worship is subject of complaints and what events/practices triggered noise reports.
Interview neighbors and religious leaders about coexistence challenges and any mediation efforts.

themes_detail.label: Garbage Disposal Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 17 LAST WEEK—a 127% increase over 8-week baseline (17 vs. 7.5 avg)—indicating possible sanitation service gaps, contamination issues, or new waste management problems.
evidence: Residential Disposal Complaint: 17 complaints last week vs. 7.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.48)
Community Board budget requests include recurring 'Other capital budget request for DEP,' suggesting persistent sanitation infrastructure gaps
Dirty Condition complaints remain high overall (631 in last 90 days), correlating with disposal issues
reporting_angles: Are collection schedules disrupted or containers inadequate for district density? Interview Sanitation Department.
Are specific buildings or blocks affected? Map complaints to identify hotspots and interview affected residents.

themes_detail.label: Sewage Backup Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Indoor sewage complaints hit 3 THREE WEEKS AGO—a 1100% spike above 8-week baseline (3 vs. 0.2 avg)—potentially signaling aging infrastructure failure, blockage, or weather-related backup affecting multiple units.
evidence: Indoor Sewage: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
Signal is 3 weeks old; current status unclear—investigate if complaints have continued or resolved
Community Board budget requests include recurring 'Other capital budget request for DEP,' indicating known infrastructure investment needs
reporting_angles: Were sewage backups concentrated in specific blocks or buildings? Request DEP service records and historical complaints.
Interview affected residents about duration, health impacts, and landlord response; check if repairs were completed.

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 9 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 700% increase above 8-week baseline (9 vs. 1.1 avg)—suggesting either sudden proliferation of unlicensed vendors, parking violations, or sanitation violations in specific commercial corridors.
evidence: Mobile Food Vendor: 9 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)
Signal is 2 weeks old; current week data needed to determine if trend continues
Greenpoint/Williamsburg has active commercial corridors (Bedford Ave, McCarty Park) where vendor activity is visible
reporting_angles: Are complaints about unlicensed vendors, parking violations, or unsanitary food handling? Request DOHMH and DOF enforcement data.
Interview commercial corridor residents and business owners about vendor impacts.
